bluf: Aira is an independent Milton Keynes performance agency selling SEO, digital PR, paid media, HubSpot CRM and CRO to mid market and B2B buyers. It is doing what its record shows: link and coverage led digital PR (Uswitch 200+ links) with SEO behind it. Where it is going the record does not say: no dated moves, no AI posture, no pricing model, and a live site that returned 403 so the read comes from a June 2026 archive capture. The one thing a rival should know: it sells paid search and paid social with no ads of its own on record, and its sitemap shows nothing updated in 90 days.
doing:
Aira positions itself as a Milton Keynes multi channel performance agency spanning SEO, digital PR, paid media, HubSpot CRM and CRO, promising growth measured in leads and revenue: in plain words, a mid market search and PR shop that added paid media and a HubSpot practice to sell the whole funnel to B2B buyers. Its headline claim is Protectivity new business up 172% and Veriff hitting 88% of its annual revenue target in nine months; both are the agency's own claims and no case study in the record describes the method.

The sold mix leads with content and digital PR (scored 3) and SEO (also 3). The evidence is concrete: digital PR cases dominate, with Uswitch at 200+ links and RS Components at 1,100+ pieces of coverage, and it publishes a State of Link Building report, a State of Technical SEO report and a Link Building Book. Behind those sit B2B and ABM (scored 2: an account based marketing page and four B2B homepage cases including Apteco MQLs up 72%), email and CRM (scored 2: a HubSpot Diamond partner badge and a Hybrid Air Vehicles HubSpot onboarding case) and paid search (scored 2: Kidscape PPC conversions up 362%, Cranfield paid search, a Premier Google Partner badge). Moz Recommended is the third listed partner. No proprietary product is listed.

AI posture: none in the record. AI search and AI automation both score 0 and the sitemap holds 0 AI URLs, the conspicuous absence for its archetype. The moves list is empty: no dated acquisition, hire, launch or rebrand, and no news, case studies or jobs were captured, in part because the live site returned 403 and the record was scored from a June 2026 Internet Archive capture. Pricing signals: none. Also absent for a performance agency of its kind: paid social, programmatic, retail media and web build evidence.
clients:
The record types the Aira client base as mid market, with verticals of B2B SaaS and technology, insurance, financial services and lending, charities, higher education, retail and ecommerce, automotive, travel and telecoms, and aerospace and engineering. Its home market is the UK: the only office listed is Milton Keynes and the homepage badges are UK Paid Media Awards 2023 and UK Search Awards 2022.

The needs read lists 18 clients, 2 with observed work and 16 named only. Kidscape came for paid performance, the signal being a case study slug about a 362% increase in conversions on its PPC campaigns. Cranfield came for organic demand and paid performance, the signal being a case study on centralising paid search to support cross faculty student recruitment. The observed mix is therefore paid performance first (share 0.6) and organic demand second (share 0.4).

The other 16 are case study pages or slugs with nothing about the work in the record: Protectivity, Veriff, Apteco, Hoxton Mix, Hagerty UK, Uswitch, RS Components, AppJobs, TECHNIA, Hybrid Air Vehicles, UNCLE, Cashmere Centre, Just Tyres, Mitie, TravelSIM and PostBeyond, all names only. For these the need is inferred from the sold mix, SEO and digital PR first, and the record does not describe the engagements. One client is shared: Uswitch also sits on the book of jbh.

What the base needs next: the Horus read places the mix best for KJ8 (human provenance becomes a distribution signal) and KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), both driven by its digital PR line, and most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out). It is likely, with moderate confidence, that this B2B heavy book will ask for citation and AI visibility reporting alongside links, a service the record shows Aira does not sell.
house:
Say and do: the Radar tested three sold lines against the house and 1 of 3 came through. Paid search is contradicted: it sells paid search and the Transparency Center holds no Google ads of its own (count 0, none in the last 30 days). LinkedIn advertising is contradicted: it sells paid social and B2B demand generation and no LinkedIn ads of its own were found; the record notes that the 322 ads matching the name query belong to other advertisers, including a near name Aira GROUP. Publishing cadence is corroborated, meaning the record confirms idleness: the sitemap lists 224 URLs, 0 updated in 90 days and 7 in 365.

The stack is WordPress with GTM and Hotjar; no social pixels, testing tools or ABM stack were detected. No llms.txt, no AI crawlers blocked, 0 AI URLs. The two flagged gaps are the missing Google and LinkedIn ads, both on lines it sells.
market:
The Horus read scores Aira at a tailwind index of -5.1, band Neutral. Best placed for KJ8 (human provenance becomes a distribution signal) and KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation), both carried by content and digital PR. Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out), where SEO, digital PR and paid search all count against it, and KJ4 (the platforms are absorbing the execution layer). Best scenario fit is The Toll Road at 43/100. Moves: partial on P4 (supply the inputs automation runs on) and P7 (owned audience hedges), absent on P1, P2, P6 and P8, unknown on P5 pricing, P3 not applicable.

The Monsoon read: index 57.8, band Onshore wind; migration 55.3 against displacement 60.3. The verdict puts 55 of the index on the sold mix, with SEO (18) and digital PR (11) the most movable hours, and sends the work 65% to South and Southeast Asia, 20% to Eastern Europe and 15% to Africa and the Maghreb, all inferred: no hub office or onshore claim is listed.
openings:
The strongest opening is the paid line. Aira sells paid search and paid social while its record shows no Google or LinkedIn ads of its own, no first party data or measurement depth, and no sign of testing ads inside AI assistants. It is likely, with moderate confidence, that a rival showing its own live campaigns and an assistant ad test with holdouts can take the paid budget from Kidscape and Cranfield, its two observed paid clients. Falsifier: a Transparency Center or LinkedIn record showing Aira campaigns under its own name.

Second, the idle house: 0 sitemap URLs updated in 90 days and 7 in 365 from an agency selling content, digital PR and SEO; a rival with a visible cadence and a citation share number leads with that, which likely holds until Aira publishes an AI visibility product.

Third, 16 of 18 clients are names only; Uswitch already sits on the jbh book and is a roughly even chance to be contestable. Fourth, no public pricing model: an outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot hold in public, and the Monsoon displacement read of 60.3 (inferred) invites an offshore delivered undercut on SEO and digital PR.
watch: I8, holdco Q3 organic growth, headcount and pricing model disclosures, next reading October 2026: output or outcome pricing announced at a top five holdco would sharpen the KJ6 exposure of Aira's hour based mix.

I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures, next reading late October 2026: search and other growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the SEO line, while above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and makes the absent P8 test costlier.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility, next reading late October 2026: US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk behind KJ1.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, next reading 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas would strengthen the KJ8 tailwind for its human authored digital PR.
No dated move sits in the record to follow up; the first thing to check is whether the live site stops returning 403 so the June 2026 Internet Archive read can be replaced with a current crawl.
The next Radar compile refreshes offices, ads, sitemap cadence and clients; this dossier is only as fresh as the 2026-09-28 compile.
